texts.preamble: State Of Gujarat-For & On Behalf Of S A ... vs Abdulkadar Mohmmedjamal Haradvala on 26 April, 2018 Author: G.R.Udhwani Bench: G.R.Udhwani R/Cr.A/1515/2010 Judgment In The High Court Of Gujarat At Ahmedabad R/Criminal Appeal No. 1515 of 2010 For Approval And Signature: Honourable Mr.Justice G.R.Udhwani ============================================
texts.facts: on 22.06.2005, which was reported to be adulterated in the report of the public analyst at Exh.-40. 3. On the label of the packaged food article several details including the marketer of the food article namely, Indu Oil Company were found. When the Food Inspector made inquiry under Section 14A from the vendor of the food article, he learnt that the same was purchased by him from Sheth Enterprise and on inquiry with Sheth Enterprise he learnt that it was purchased from Sheth Oil Industries. Sheth Oil Industries further came out with a case that the food article marketed by Indu Oil Company was not sold by it to Sheth Enterpise but the one marketed by Thirumalai Agencies was sold by it to Sheth Enterprise. In other words, it was case of the Sheth Oil Industries that the food article in question was not sold by it to Sheth Enterprise. 4. The Food Inspector did not receive any co-operation from Indu Oil Company even as he kept on inquiring on four or five occasions with the said company, under Section 14A of the Act. Eventually, he filed the complaint. 5. Learned APP has assailed the impugned judgment and order on the ground that none of the entities above referred were entitled to the benefit under Section 14A in absence of their giving R/CR.A/1515/2010 JUDGMENT complete information with batch number and other facts leading to the identity of the food article in question, to the Food Inspector.
texts.arguments: It was contended that Sheth Oil Industries took the stand above referred only to save Indu Oil Company and the Indu Oil Company did not come out with any details under Section 14A of the Act. 5.1 It was contended that the Court erroneously found that the sanction suffers from non-application of mind inasmuch as on not less than three occasions the authority after looking into the papers declined sanction and eventually when it found that no case is made out against Thirumalai Agencies, it refused the sanction qua the said entity and granted it for prosecuting other entities. 6. Learned counsel for the respondents while urging for the sustainance of the impugned judgment and order would contend that whole quantity of 5 kg. of the food article i.e. coconut oil was not throughly stirred and thus the sample was not a representative sample and the accused must be given the benefit of doubt as indicated in Criminal Revision Application No.593 of 2005 [2008 (1) FAC 381]. State Of Gujarat-For & On Behalf Of S A ... vs Abdulkadar Mohmmedjamal Haradvala on 26 April, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77058516/ 2 6.1 It was also contended that in absence of joining the manufacturer the complaint was not maintainable. The learned counsel also contended that the food article could have been best used within 12 months from the date of manufacture and the sample was collected on 09.08.2004 and the complaint was lodged only on 15.02.2007 and by the time the best before date had gone and the food article was no more good for human consumption and therefore, the right of the respondents to get the sample re- analyzed as contemplated in Section 13(2B) of the Act, has been denied. R/CR.A/1515/2010 JUDGMENT 7.
